result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.count_triangles()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Count triangles containing each node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L10183-L10255){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.count_triangles() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns the number of triangles that include each node in the graph. For undirected graphs, counts each triangle once per node. For directed graphs, counts directed triangles (closed triplets). A triangle is a set of three nodes where all three pairs are connected. This is the smallest non-trivial cycle and a fundamental measure of local clustering in networks. Time complexity: `O(m * d_max)` where `m` is edges and `d_max` is maximum degree. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping node IDs to triangle counts. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Count triangles in a simple triangle: ::: {#b8de6a8a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") ) counts = graph.count_triangles() # Returns node IDs: {node_id_a: 1, node_id_b: 1, node_id_c: 1} # Convert to labels if needed counts_by_label = {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): count for nid, count in counts.items()} # Returns {"A": 1, "B": 1, "C": 1} counts_by_label ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': 1, 'C': 1, 'B': 1} ``` ::: ::: Count triangles in a more complex graph: ::: {#17bf0e8d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Graph with 2 triangles sharing an edge graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") .add_edge(source="C", target="A") # Triangle 1 .add_edge(source="B", target="D") .add_edge(source="D", target="C") # Triangle 2 with B-C ) counts = graph.count_triangles() # Returns node IDs: B and C each participate in 2 triangles # Convert to labels for display - iteration example for node_id, count in counts.items(): label = graph.get_label_from_id(node_id) # Each iteration shows:
